version.changelog: Republish the current skill package with schema_version 2 guidance, recent command coverage, export --force guidance, and OpenClaw metadata version 1.3.1.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: clipboard-memory
Version: 1.3.1

The skill provides an interface to a local archive of all macOS clipboard history (via the `clipmem` tool), which inherently involves high-risk access to sensitive data such as passwords, tokens, and private documents. While the behavior aligns with the stated purpose, the `scripts/check-setup.sh` script employs risky patterns, including the use of `eval` on output processed from external command results. Furthermore, the skill grants the agent the ability to export binary data (images, PDFs) to arbitrary local paths and restore previous clipboard states, which could be leveraged for data manipulation or exfiltration if the agent is targeted by prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill does what it says: it requires the local clipmem binary and uses it to read, export, restore, and manage a local macOS clipboard archive; nothing requested or installed is disproportionate to that purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the requested artifacts: the skill requires only the clipmem binary (installed via Homebrew or cargo) and reads the local clipmem SQLite archive. No unrelated cloud credentials, services, or system-wide secrets are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are narrowly scoped to running clipmem commands, checking watcher health, exporting raw bytes, restoring the clipboard, and deleting/purging snapshots. This includes writing exported binary content to user-specified file paths and managing a background capture service — expected for clipboard-recovery functionality but worth noting because it can export potentially sensitive content to disk and perform irreversible deletes (forget / purge).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Install steps point to a Homebrew formula (tristanmanchester/tap/clipmem) and offer a cargo install alternative. Homebrew tap is a third-party tap (not necessarily official core); this is plausible for a niche tool but users should verify the tap's trustworthiness before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables or external credentials are required. The only filesystem access implied (and documented) is the clipmem SQLite DB at ~/Library/Application Support/clipmem/clipmem.sqlite3, which is proportional to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and does not request special platform-wide privileges. It relies on a background watcher (LaunchAgent or Homebrew service) to capture clipboard events — this is part of the intended design and is documented in the SKILL.md and setup checks.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent with its stated purpose, but before installing: (1) confirm the Homebrew tap or cargo package is from a source you trust; (2) understand that clipmem archives every clipboard event (including passwords, tokens, or sensitive text) into a local SQLite DB — review retention/ignore-list settings and prune or disable capture if you need stricter privacy; (3) exported content will be written to disk (choose safe output paths) and forget/purge operations permanently remove snapshots; (4) the skill requires a background service (LaunchAgent or brew service) to be running for live capture — follow the provided setup checks if results look empty.
